blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Picture-description dementia classification uses a shared visual scene, but a transcript-level prediction alone does not identify the scene evidence underlying its inputs. NarraSpace links words and speech times to named picture elements and retrieves utterances for predefined scene events. Narrative-spatial descriptors summarize coverage and temporal organization. A frozen language model contrasts each event's text under examples from Alzheimer's disease and healthy-control training participants, alongside transcript surprisal and coverage measurements. Retained source records link event scores to their source utterances, speech intervals, and lexical matches. On the official 48-participant test set of the Alzheimer's Dementia Recognition through Spontaneous Speech benchmark, a fixed support vector classifier achieves $80.88\%\pm2.56\%$ mean accuracy over fifty seeds; averaged probabilities yield $81.25\%$ accuracy and $91.32\%$ area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. NarraSpace makes the construction of scene-linked classification inputs explicit and inspectable by connecting event-indexed language-model measurements to their source utterances, speech timing, and extraction records. Such source-linked measurements could support clinician review of picture descriptions by presenting quantitative summaries alongside the original speech evidence.
blocks.zh: 图片描述性痴呆症分类使用共享的视觉场景,但单是笔录级预测并不能识别其输入的场景证据. 纳拉 空间将文字和语音时间链接到命名的图片元素,并检索预定义的场景事件的语音. 描述-空间描述摘要介绍覆盖面和时间组织。 一个冷冻的语言模型在阿尔茨海默氏病和健康控制培训参与者的例子下对比了每个事件的文字,同时对比了记录片的附加和覆盖测量. 保留源记录将事件分数与源词,语音间隔,和词典匹配联系起来. 在通过自发语音基准确认阿尔茨海默氏痴呆症的官方48参与测试集上,一个固定的辅助矢量分类器在50个种子上达到80.88\%\pm2.56\%$的平均精度;平均概率为81.25\%$精度,在接收器操作特征曲线下达到91.32\%$. 纳拉 空间通过将事件索引语言模型测量与其源词、语音时间和提取记录连接起来,使场景相关分类投入的构建明确和可以检查。 这种与源相连的测量可以支持临床医生对图片描述的审查,方法是在陈述原始证据的同时提出定量摘要。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Picture-description dementia classification has a useful constraint: the picture supplies a shared reference for what a participant could describe. In the Alzheimer’s Dementia Recognition through Spontaneous Speech (ADReSS) benchmark, every participant describes the Cookie Theft scene ( Luz et al., 2020 ) . Descriptions differ in the objects mentioned, their order, the time spent describing them, and the relations expressed. Clinical picture-description assessment counts information units: depicted objects, actions, and facts conveyed by the speaker ( Goodglass et al., 2001 ; Croisile et al., 1996 ; Fraser et al., 2016 ) . These analyses suggest a representation question: how can a classifier’s input retain the connection between a linguistic measurement and the particular scene content from which it was obtained?
blocks.zh: 图片描述性痴呆症分类有一个有用的制约:图片为参与者可以描述的内容提供了共同的参考. 在阿尔茨海默通过自发演讲(ADRESS)确认痴呆症的基准中,每位参与者都描述了Cookie Theft场景(Luz等人,2020年)。 描述在提到的物体,它们的顺序,描述它们所花的时间,以及表达的关系上各不相同. 临床图片描述评估计算信息单位:演讲者所讲述的物体、行动和事实(Goodglass等人,2001年;Croisile等人,1996年;Fraser等人,2016年)。 这些分析表明一个表述问题:分类员的投入如何能保留语言计量与从中获得的特定场景内容之间的联系?

blocks.en: Acoustic and linguistic features, pretrained representations, and whole-transcript language-model scores provide useful classification signals ( Yuan et al., 2021 ; Martinc et al., 2021 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Xiao et al., 2025 ) . A scalar score, however, does not itself identify the phrase, event, or scene location associated with that signal. Prior work already represents picture descriptions as spatio-semantic paths, aligns spoken words with image regions, and models image–text consistency ( Ambadi et al., 2021 ; Heidarzadeh & Ratté, 2023 ; Ng et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2025 ) . The connection we study is between an event in the picture, its retrieved utterances, and their likelihood under class-derived example contexts. Keeping these together allows the score and its extraction choices to be inspected.
blocks.zh: 声学和语言特征,预受考验的表示,和全调语言模型分数提供了有用的分类信号(袁等,2021;马丁克等,2021;王等,2023;萧等,2025.). 然而,标分本身并不能识别与该信号相关的短语、事件或场景位置。 先前的工作已经将图片描述为:斯皮提-语义路径,将口语与图像区域相协调,以及模型图像-文本一致性(Ambadi等人,2021年;Heidarzadeh & Ratté, 2023; Ng等, 2025b; Li等, 2025.). 我们研究的关联在于图片中的某一事件,其检索到的语句,以及它们根据类出例环境的可能性. 保持这些优势可以检查得分及其提取选择。

blocks.en: NarraSpace constructs an evidence representation around a fixed scene schema. It links words to speech intervals and fifteen named picture elements (scene anchors), retrieves utterances for seven predefined events, and contrasts the same retrieved text under examples from Alzheimer’s disease and healthy-control training participants using one frozen language model. A conventional classifier combines this evidence with speech, linguistic, and image–text descriptors. Retained source records allow a reader to move from a displayed event score back to its utterances, lexical matches, and scene anchors. This is source attribution : it specifies where evidence came from. It is distinct from attributing a classifier’s decision to individual features or demonstrating that an explanation improves clinical judgment.
blocks.zh: NarraSpace围绕固定的场景方案构建了证据表述. 它把文字与语音间隔和15个命名的图片元素(景色锚地)联系起来,检索7个预先定义的事件的言论,并利用一个冷冻的语言模型,将阿尔茨海默病的例子和健康的控制培训参与者对比出来。 传统分类法将这种证据与语言、语言和图像文本描述法结合起来。 保留源记录允许读者从所显示的事件分数回移到它的语句,词汇匹配和场景主播. 这是来源归属:它规定了证据的来源。 它不同于将分类者的决定归结为个人特征或证明解释能改善临床判断。

blocks.en: Our contribution connects scene structure, event-indexed language-model measurements, and source records. We provide (1) a representation separating anchor trajectories, event retrieval, and classification features; (2) paired likelihood measurements for retrieved utterances, alongside scene-token and coverage descriptors; and (3) an assessment with shared transcript processing, family removals, participant-level uncertainty, and auditable cases. The event index lets a reader locate a measurement’s source and inspect its extraction choices. Whether this organization improves inspection accuracy or speed over simple retrieval remains an empirical question.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献将场景结构、事件索引语言模型测量和源记录联系起来。 我们提供(1) 将主机轨迹、事件检索和分类特征分开的说明;(2) 与现场记录和覆盖描述符一起,对检索的言论进行对接的可能性测量;和(3) 用共享记录、家庭迁移、参与者的不确定性和可审计案例进行评估。 事件指数让读者找到测量的源头并检查其提取选择。 这个组织是否比简单的检索提高检查的准确性或速度仍然是一个经验性问题。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: ADReSS standardizes picture-description classification with an official participant split ( Luz et al., 2020 ) . Relevant representations include linguistic and acoustic descriptors, temporal integration, pause-aware language models, ensembles, and prompt learning ( Fraser et al., 2016 ; Yuan et al., 2021 ; Syed et al., 2021 ; Martinc et al., 2021 ; Wang et al., 2023 ) . Word-level multimodal alignment provides another route to relating the speech signal to its transcription ( Ortiz-Perez et al., 2025 ) . Transcript construction matters: manual and automatic transcripts, annotation handling, and retained disfluencies can change the information available to a model ( Liu et al., 2025 ) . We use official participant transcripts and specify their normalization to make the input available to each feature family explicit.
blocks.zh: ADReSS将图象描述分类标准化,将正式参与者分成两部分(Luz等人,2020年)。 相关表述包括语言和声学描述词,时间融合,暂停-意识语言模型,综艺,和即时学习(Fraser等,2016;Yuan等,2021;Syed等,2021;Martinc等,2021;Wang等,2023). 文字层面的多式统一为将语音信号与其转录联系起来提供了另一种途径(Ortiz-Perez等,2025年)。 转写施工事项:人工和自动笔录,注解处理,以及所保留的疏漏,可以将现有信息改为模型(刘等,2025. 我们使用正式的与会者笔录,并具体说明这些笔录的正常化,使每个专题家庭都能得到明确的投入。

blocks.en: Spatio-semantic graphs encode paths through picture information units ( Ambadi et al., 2021 ; Ng et al., 2025b ) . A separate study by Ng et al. (2025a) learns information-unit detection and ordering with a pretrained text encoder, evaluating both against human annotations and validating derived features externally. Word–region alignment, eye movements, image–text relevance, and topic evolution also connect descriptions to scenes ( Heidarzadeh & Ratté, 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2025 ) . NarraSpace builds on this structural premise: its fixed event records index class-context likelihood measurements and their source utterances.
blocks.zh: Spatio-语义图通过图片信息单元编码路径(Ambadi等,2021;Ng等,2025b.). Ng等人(2025a)单独进行的一项研究学习了信息单元检测和订购,并使用经过预先训练的文本编码器,同时对照人类说明进行评价并外部验证衍生特征. Word-region,眼动,图像-文字关联,和主题演化也将描述与场景相接(Heidarzadeh & Ratté,2023;Wang等,2024;Zhu等,2023;Li等,2025). 纳拉 空间建立在这一结构前提上:其固定事件记录指数级-文本概率测量及其源词.

blocks.en: Xiao et al. (2025) contrast whole-transcript perplexities from class-conditioned models. Zhu et al. (2024) use training-derived feature context, including picture content, for adversarial generation and perplexity-based detection; Su et al. (2026) study demonstration-centered anchoring. NarraSpace applies class-derived contexts within one frozen model to event text and retains each contrast’s source. The event, scored text, contrast, and extraction rules are available together for inspection. This measurement-level contribution complements the decision explanations studied in clinician-facing systems ( Ntampakis et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 萧等. (2025)与类条件型号的全画幅偏差形成对比. 朱等编. (2024)使用由培训衍生的特征上下文,包括图片内容,用于对抗生成和基于迷惑的检测;Su等 (2026)研究以演示为主锚. 纳拉 空间在一个被冻结的模型中将类派背景用于事件文本并保留每个对比源。 活动、评分文本、对比和提取规则一起可供检查。 这种衡量水平的贡献补充了临床医生-培养系统所研究的决定解释(Ntampakis等,2025年)。

blocks.zh: 3.1 输入、场景锁定和事件检索

blocks.en:
The inputs are audio, the official transcript, and the shared Cookie Theft
image. Transcript processing has two branches. Language-model scoring uses
participant speech after removing examiner turns, task instructions, annotation
markers, and angle-bracketed retraced text, including its words; retained
spoken forms are not replaced by standard-form corrections. Linguistic
features additionally use the original morphological and grammatical
annotations and raw disfluency markers. WhisperX forced alignment attaches
word times to the cleaned participant text without generating a new transcript ( Bain et al., 2023 ) .

from the prompt; weights are not fine-tuned. This is supervised context

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
The shared picture provides a reference for connecting what a participant
says with how the description unfolds. NarraSpace uses scene anchors to
organize the timed word sequence and events to index retrieved utterances
and their class-context likelihood contrasts. Its contribution lies in
keeping these measurements connected to the speech and extraction choices
that produced them. A reader can examine the wording behind a score,
inspect a mapping between words and scene anchors, and identify text shared
by several events. These connections make the construction of classification
inputs explicit and available for review.

blocks.en:
The empirical findings show why measurement construction and predictive
performance need to be examined together. Removing narrative-spatial features
lowers mean accuracy, while the compact alternative performs differently
across mean and aggregated accuracy. The likelihood stream changes which
participants are classified correctly even when aggregate accuracy is
unchanged. These observations motivate examining the selected features and
participant decisions alongside overall metrics; their paired uncertainty
estimates are reported in the appendices. Source records support this
examination at the level of input construction. Attributing a prediction to
a particular measurement additionally requires analysis of the fitted
classifier and its threshold.

The present evaluation is exploratory, using one English-language benchmark
with prior test exposure. The mapping audit assesses accepted anchor
assignments; direct event-level annotation and same-model comparisons of
local and whole-transcript scoring would test further aspects of the
representation. Independent participant cohorts would assess transfer beyond
this setting. For clinical research, source-linked measurements could help
reviewers examine quantitative summaries alongside the original speech,
including the wording and timing associated with a scene event. Evaluating
that use requires measuring inspection accuracy and effort, followed by
assessment of its contribution to clinical judgment.

blocks.en:
NarraSpace connects scene structure, event-indexed language-model
measurements, and speech timing in a representation whose sources remain
available for inspection. On the official 48-participant test set, the fixed
classifier achieves 80.88 % 80.88\% mean accuracy over fifty seeds and 81.25 % 81.25\% accuracy after probability aggregation. Feature controls and participant-level
comparisons characterize how the representation affects classification,

picture descriptions through both quantitative summaries and their original
speech evidence, with a concrete route toward evaluating their use in
human review.

blocks.en:
Self-exclusion removes every span from the participant being scored from
both class pools, including when that participant belongs to a classifier’s
training set. Fold exclusion additionally prevents any validation participant
from contributing exemplars to any feature used to train or validate
the classifier in that fold. A single precomputed matrix whose rows were
individually scored out of fold does not necessarily satisfy this second
requirement after repartitioning: a training row’s context may have contained
a participant now in validation. The classifier training and validation rows
must therefore use the same explicitly defined outer-training exemplar pool,
with additional per-target self-exclusion where applicable.

blocks.en:
The participant transcript is also scored under its own preceding textual
context. Fixed object, actor, action, and vague-term lexicons select token
positions in two steps: first match full words to these lexicons, then include
subwords whose character intervals lie wholly within the matched word intervals.
Unlike cloze selection, this step does not independently match each subword
surface to a filler lexicon. With surprisal u j = − log ⁡ p θ ​ ( x j ∣ x < j ) u_{j}=-\log p_{\theta}(x_{j}\mid x_{<j}) , the descriptors are mean, maximum,
and variance over the union of object, actor, and action positions, plus mean
surprisal over vague, action, and object positions separately. These six
values use transcript context and scene-lexicon selection; they are not
exemplar-conditioned local event scores.
Transcripts longer than 256 tokens use windows of 256 with 64-token overlap
and stride 192. The first window emits its scored positions; later windows
emit positions after their 64-token overlap, so every scored transcript
token contributes once. The first transcript token has no preceding context
and its undefined score is excluded from finite-score summaries.

blocks.en:
Likelihood matching lowercases tokens, strips boundary punctuation, and
applies the first eligible suffix rule in the order ies , ied , ing , ed , es , er , and s . This is the normalization used for the likelihood lexicons; anchor assignment
and event-field matching have their own rules. A word matched by one channel
is therefore not automatically a match in another. It has no irregular-word table or doubled-consonant recovery:
for example, running becomes runn . Consequently, a spoken
concept may fail a canonical match even when a human would recognize it.

blocks.en:
The correction fixes the historical model and all family masks before
reanalysis; it does not search configurations against test accuracy.
Only the downstream fitting and the required summaries are recomputed:
class-context language-model scores already exist for the allowed outer-fold
pools. They are filtered and reaggregated, not generated again. Table 7 separates the outer folds from the classifier’s internal probability folds.
For each of the fifty seeds and each of the five fixed outer training folds: 1. Reaggregate the four cloze and nine paired descriptors for every
training participant from persisted scores conditioned on the same held-out
fold. No participant
in that fold contributes an exemplar to any fitting or validation row. A
fitting target is additionally excluded from its own contexts. 2. Rebuild the healthy-control reference from the fitting partition only.
Exclude a fitting target from its own reference. Validation participants use
the full reference allowed by that fold. 3. Apply the fixed family mask. Fit likelihood medians and missingness
augmentation, supervised top-sixty selection, standardization, and the
support vector classifier using fitting rows only. Predict the held-out rows. Concatenating the five validation predictions gives one probability for each
of the 108 training participants. The final classifier uses all 108 rows,
with each row’s own held-out-fold likelihood and healthy-control reference.
The 48 test rows use full-training contexts and the full-training control
reference. All final preprocessing quantities are fitted on the 108 training
rows. Thus, the final fitting and test rows use different reference-pool
sizes; the correction does not claim to eliminate this distributional
difference.
